Subject: Re: High error / timeouts impacting checkout (URGENT)

Triage update / findings:
- Root cause (prelim): a combination of a slow KV cache warm-up after a regional autoscaling event + a spike in long-context requests from a third-party integration. The slow warm-up increased per-request token processing time which caused queue backlog; the autoscaler reacted but lagged and generated transient 429s.
- No code deploys at 08:40; rolling work happened earlier in the night but outside affected pool.

Immediate mitigations applied (08:55 PT):
- Enabled model fallback for MercadoHealth routes to a lower-latency quantized variant (reduces median token time ~30%)
- Increased short-term capacity threshold for their dedicated pool and forced an extra warm-up sweep on KV caches
- Temporarily limited incoming burst size via per-route throttling while we stabilize

Customer impact: 60 minutes of elevated errors; most traffic started recovering after 09:10 PT. We left fallback and throttles in place until full warm-up completed.

Next actions (owners):
- (dev_patel) Add a pre-warm KV cache step to autoscaler lifecycle for tenant pools — P1, ETA 2 days to ship canary.
- (monica_patel) Update runbook to include an immediate model-fallback checklist and a standard short-term credit offer for impacted customers — P1, ETA 1 day for runbook patch, 2 days to finalize credit language.
- (marcus_lin) Evaluate SLO thresholds and alert thresholds for retry amplification detection; propose tuning — P2, ETA 5 business days.
- (sean_gallagher) Coordinate exec-facing summary and offer (credit/discount) to MercadoHealth — P1, today.

I'll drop logs and a concise RCA in the shared drive link.

- Dev

Summary / executive ask:
Thanks team — good triage. A few additional asks from my side to make this exec-ready and prevent recurrence:
1) Alerting: add an aggregated alert that combines rising 429s + 95th latency delta + retry amplification score so we get earlier signal than raw 5xx counts. (Owner: marcus_lin, ETA: 3 days)
2) Runbooks: Monica to publish a short immediate-response runbook (3 steps max) for sales/solutions engineers to execute during customer-impact events. Include exact steps to enable model fallback, throttle, and escalate to SRE. (Owner: monica_patel, ETA: 1 day)
3) Capacity/autoscaling: dev to implement pre-warm sweep and add a fast-path to scale up worker warmers for tenant pools to avoid KV cold starts. (Owner: dev_patel, ETA: 48 hours for canary)
4) SLO tuning: we should review MercadoHealth contract SLOs (p95/p99) and propose a short-term uplift in headroom for peak traffic windows. Also recommend a guardrail that prevents client SDKs from blind retries beyond X attempts. (Owner: marcus_lin + sean_gallagher, ETA: 5 days)
5) Customer communications: Sean to send an executive update including the mitigation steps we applied, proposed credits, and a timeline for follow-ups. (Owner: sean_gallagher, ETA: today)

I'll review the post-incident report once Monica and Dev upload artifacts. Marcus

Subject: MercadoHealth incident — mitigation summary & next steps

Elena — following up with a concise summary and commitments from Redwood: 

What happened: transient spike in 5xx/429 due to KV cache warm-up overlap with a third-party long-context spike; this led to queueing and retry amplification.
What we did: enabled model fallback, increased dedicated pool warmers, applied short-term throttles; system recovered and error rates returned to baseline within ~60 minutes.
What we'll do: implement a pre-warm step in autoscaling lifecycle (canary in 48h), publish a 3-step customer-facing runbook, add composite alerting for early detection, and review SLO thresholds and recommended retry guardrails.
Compensation: recommended one month of service credit on an opt-in basis while we finalize improvements (open to discussion).
Timeline: runbook and customer communication — 24 hours; pre-warm canary — 48 hours; SLO/alert tuning proposals — 5 business days.

If this aligns, we'll schedule a short sync with your platform team to walk the technical plan. Appreciate the quick coordination and patience.

— Sean
